facts.text: Humboldt began as Springvale, named for the natural springs near the Des Moines River, before adopting the name of explorer Alexander von Humboldt in 1863.
Founder Stephen Harris Taft laid out the town’s original plan in 1863, turning prairie into a planned community with wide boulevards and a sawmill.
Frank Gotch, a world‑champion wrestler, helped shape Humboldt’s identity, and a bronze statue of him stands in Bicknell Park.
Gotch Park, just south of Humboldt, once hosted prehistoric and Dakota Indian villages near the confluence of the Des Moines River’s forks.
The Carnegie Humboldt Public Library, built in 1908, remains a historic landmark in the city’s heart.
In the 1800s, the area that is now Humboldt was believed to have housed Fort Confederation, a trading post of uncertain origins.
